question: Could you analyze our data and identify which ten-year period starting from any movie release year present in the data had the largest number of films, considering consecutive ten-year periods beginning at each unique year? Only output the start year and the total count for that specific period.
sql:
-- Get the single top result
WITH movie_years AS (
    SELECT 
        MID,
        CASE 
            WHEN LENGTH(year) = 4 THEN TRY_CAST(year AS INTEGER)
            ELSE TRY_CAST(SPLIT_PART(year, ' ', 2) AS INTEGER)
        END as release_year
    FROM Movie 
),
unique_start_years AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT release_year as start_year 
    FROM movie_years 
    WHERE release_year IS NOT NULL
),
period_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        u.start_year,
        COUNT(my.MID) as film_count
    FROM unique_start_years u
    JOIN movie_years my ON my.release_year >= u.start_year AND my.release_year < u.start_year + 10
    GROUP BY u.start_year
)
SELECT start_year, film_count 
FROM period_counts 
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY film_count DESC, start_year ASC) = 1

Lookup tables define attributes: Country (CID), Genre (GID), Language (LAID), and Location (LID) provide standardized codes for names. Junction tables link movies to these attributes and people. M_Country connects Movie MID to Country CID. M_Genre links Movie MID to Genre GID. M_Language associates Movie MID with Language LAID. M_Location ties Movie MID to Location LID. M_Cast, M_Director, and M_Producer all connect Movie MID to Person PID, distinguishing roles. M_Language is effectively one-to-one with Movie, while M_Location often contains NULLs.
